payload.title: When Operators Approach Hardware Limits: Profiling-Driven Analysis of Real-Time Inference on Orin
payload.summary: This document covers compiling Flash Attention 2 on Jetson AGX Orin (SM 8.7), benchmarking FA2 vs SDPA, deep profiling of GEMM bandwidth bottlenecks, and the discovery that 67% of inference time is framework overhead rather than GPU computation.

sections.heading: 1. Background: Why SDPA Was the Only Option
sections.gist: In the previous deployment of wall-x on Orin, Flash Attention 2 failed to compile, forcing the use of SDPA.

sections.heading: 2. Why FA2 Fails to Compile on Orin
sections.gist: PyPI only ships x86_64 wheels for flash-attn.

sections.heading: 4. Benchmark: FA2 vs SDPA on Orin
sections.gist: Test configuration: wall-x 3B model, bf16, single 640×480 image, VQA prompt, max_new_tokens=64, 3 warmup + 10 timed runs, GPU locked at 1300.5 MHz.

sections.heading: 5. Why FA2 is "Only" 27% Faster
sections.gist: FA2 typically delivers 2-3x speedup on A100/H100.

sections.heading: 6. GEMM Profiling: Bandwidth Is the Bottleneck
sections.gist: Detailed breakdown of 1643ms total GEMM time (6264 calls):

sections.gist: TRT-LLM ships 180 SM 8.7-specific precompiled cubin files for fused attention, completely independent from open-source flash-attn:

```
4.3 GB ÷ 168 GB/s = 25.6 ms (bandwidth limit)
Actual GEMM time ≈ 25.7 ms/step (~72% bandwidth utilization)
```

```
Per decode step:
  Wall clock:       97.2 ms (100%)
  GPU kernel:       29.7 ms (30.6%)  ← actual computation
  Framework overhead: 67.5 ms (69.4%)  ← Python/HuggingFace idle
```
